core_obligations: The direct image (proof lines 4818-4820): by the companion result the direct image of a sheaf along a continuous functor is already a sheaf, so the sheafification in the formula for the pullback is unnecessary and the pullback is computed by evaluating at the image object.
The left adjoint (proof lines 4821-4822): the composite of the left Kan extension with sheafification is left adjoint to the direct image by the companion adjunction.
Limits and colimits (proof lines 4823-4824): the assertion about commutation follows from the general properties of adjoint functors.
proof_roadmap: Use that the direct image of a sheaf is a sheaf, so no sheafification is needed.
Identify the left adjoint of the direct image.
Read off the commutation with limits and colimits from the adjunction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a functor which is both cocontinuous and continuous the sheafification in the formula for the pullback of the associated morphism of topoi is unnecessary, that the pullback has a left adjoint obtained by sheafifying the left Kan extension, and that the pullback commutes with arbitrary limits and colimits (statement lines 4794-4815). The proof is short and complete: the direct image of a sheaf along a continuous functor is a sheaf by the companion result, which removes the sheafification and identifies the pullback on objects (proof lines 4818-4820); the left adjoint is identified through the companion adjunction (proof lines 4821-4822); and the assertion about limits and colimits follows from the general properties of adjoint functors (proof lines 4823-4824). The non-formal content is the removal of the sheafification. The claim is H1: a short argument with each input named.
